Phase 2 · Approval gate

Build & Challenge

Turn the approved view into portfolios, then try to break them.

Decision question

Does each portfolio earn its place inside the client mandate after costs, constraints, and the bear case?

Translate the Phase 1 view into capital-market expectations, construct client portfolios, select securities, design risk mitigation, and challenge each recommendation under stress.

Committee motion

Motion to approve the proposed portfolio and risk-mitigation plan for each assigned client.

Workstreams

A · Capital-market expectations

Convert the market view into expected returns, volatility, correlations, and Solver constraints for base and bear cases.

B · Securities & implementation

Select and weight securities, document macro and client fit, and compare at least two risk-mitigation approaches.

C · Stress test & corrective action

Run the bear case, test the tripwire, quantify hedge effects, and document trades required to cure any breach.

Required evidence

  • Base and bear CME inputs with cited rationale
  • Solver output and constraint checks for each client
  • Security-selection table with macro connection, client fit, weight, and source
  • Risk-mitigation comparison showing cost and trade-offs
  • Stress-test result against each approved tripwire
  • Before/after record for any corrective trades
  • AI audit entries linked to human verification
  • Phase 2 decision record signed by all four members

Committee responsibilities

Committee seatResponsibility in Phase 2
Client and Macro StrategistTest whether proposed allocations and securities fit the approved client mandate and the committee's market view.
Fixed-Income AnalystAnalyze yields, duration, credit, liquidity, and structure; recommend fixed-income exposures that meet the approved guardrails.
Fund and ETF AnalystEvaluate funds and ETFs using objective, holdings, benchmark, fees, liquidity, tax efficiency, and tracking evidence.
Portfolio Manager and Risk AnalystIntegrate the allocation, run bear-case stress tests, compare mitigants, identify breaches, and require corrective action.

Approval standard

Gate 2

Approve, revise, or reject each client portfolio. A failed tripwire cannot receive approval without a documented correction.

The decision record must state the motion, evidence reviewed, each member's vote, any dissent or reservation, and the owner and due date for every required revision.
